$comment: ONE number, read by check:ci-agent-session-archival and by nothing else --
yet. It is in a file rather than in the gate for the reason every other
retention in .ci/config is: the number is a judgment call that will be
retuned, and a retune must not be a code change.
grace_days is STACKED ON TOP of the hook's own abandonment horizon,
WORKLIST_DEAD_HOURS (24h), which wl_store.agent_state_dead applies and this
gate reuses rather than redefines. A session's agent/<session>/ directory
becomes a finding once it is ABANDONED by that oracle AND grace_days have
passed on top -- roughly 15 days idle in total at the value below.
WHY A GRACE PERIOD AT ALL, rather than reding the moment a directory goes
abandoned. The 24h horizon is met by 18 of the 19 peer directories on the
tree this gate landed against. A gate keyed on it alone would red on every
unrelated PR, blaming whoever's branch runs CI next for eighteen other
sessions going idle -- a fact about the passage of time, not about a diff,
and the exact shape that gets suppressed within a day.
HOW 14 WAS CHOSEN, and what would falsify it. Long enough that ordinary
session cadence (a session paused over a long weekend, a weekly review
wave) clears the debt before the clock fires; short enough that the debt
still comes due. If routine housekeeping turns out to run less often than
every two weeks, this gate will red on unrelated PRs again, and THIS is the
line to change -- not the gate, and never an allowlist.
